nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: We fix $(y,\theta)\in\partial_+S\mathrm{M}$ and let the positive function $\Psi_\kappa$ given by (\ref{5.10}), we have \begin{multline} \Big|\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta)\Big|=\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta)\,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr \leq\quad \Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi) \Big(\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta) -\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\xi)\Big) \,d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|\cr +\Big| \displaystyle\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1} \Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\xi) d\omega_y(\xi)\Big|. \end{multline} Since we have $$ \Big|\displaystyle \mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta)-\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\xi)\Big|\leq C \,|\theta-\xi|, $$ then we deduce upon applying Lemma \ref{L.5.2} with $\Psi=\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\cdot)$ that we have the following estimation \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_{\kappa}(\theta,\xi)\,|\theta-\xi|\,d\omega_y(\xi)\cr +C\Big(h+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\mathrm{M})}+h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\| \Big)\|\Psi_{\kappa}\|_{H^2(S_y\mathrm{M}_1)}^{2}. \end{multline*} On the other hand, by (\ref{4.20}) and (\ref{4.19}), we obtain $$ \Big|\mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta)\Big|\leq C \,(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+C\Big( h^{-3}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\mathrm{M})}+h \Big)(1-\kappa)^{-(3+n)}. $$ Take $(1-\kappa)$ small such that $(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}=h(1-\kappa)^{-(n+3)}$, that is $(1-\kappa)=h^{2n/1+2n^2+6n}$, we find two constants $\delta>0$ and $\beta>0$ such that $$\Big| \mathcal{I}(q)(y,\theta) \Big|\leq C \Big[ h^{-\delta}\|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+ h^{-\delta}\norm{a}_{\mathcal{C}^0(\mathrm{M})}+h^{\beta} \Big].$$ The proof of Lemma \ref{L.5.3} is complete.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4: stability of the electric potential
nodes.statement: Integrating the estimate (\ref{5.11}) over $\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1,$ with respect to $ \mu(y,\theta) \, \,\mathrm{d\sigma}^{2n-2} (y,\theta)$, then minimizing on $h$, we get \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{I}(q)\|_{L^2(\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1)}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\mathrm{M})})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation} By interpolation inequality, we get \begin{align} \norm{\mathcal{I}(q)}^2_{H^1(\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1)} & \leq C \|\mathcal{I}(q)\|_{L^2(\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1)}\|\mathcal{I}(q)\|_{H^2(\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1)} \cr & \leq C \|\mathcal{I}(q)\|_{L^2(\partial_+S\mathrm{M}_1)}. \end{align} From the Theorem \ref{theorem}, it follows that \begin{equation} \|q\|_{L^2(\mathrm{M})}\leq C ( \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|+\|a\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(\mathrm{M})})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+\delta}}. \end{equation} Using the estimate (\ref{4.26}), we conclude that $$ \|q\|_{L^2(\mathrm{M})}\leq C \|\Lambda_{a_{2},q_{2}}-\Lambda_{a_{1},q_{1}}\|^{s_1}, $$ where $s_1 \in (0,1)$. This completes the proof of the Theorem \ref{Th2}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: We define the Poisson kernel of $B(0,1)\subset T_y \mathrm{M}_1$, i-e., $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\theta}^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\theta-\xi}^n},\quad \theta\in B(0,1);\,\, \xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}_1. $$ For $0<\kappa<1$, we define $\Psi_\kappa: S_y\mathrm{M}_1\times S_y\mathrm{M}_1\to \mathbb{R}$ as $$ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi)=P(\kappa\theta,\xi). $$ Let $P_0$ the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ i.e., $$ P_0(\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi})=\frac{1-\abs{\hat{\theta}}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\hat{\theta}-\hat{\xi}}_0^n},\quad \hat{\theta}\in B_0(0,1);\,\, \hat{\xi}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ where $\abs{\cdot}_0$ is the Euclidian norm of $\mathbb{R}^n$. From the well known properties of $P_0$, we have $$ \int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi}) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1, \quad\textrm{for all}\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\, \hat{\theta}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ Let $\gamma=\sqrt{\mathrm{g}}:=(\gamma_{ij})$ be definite symetric positive matrix such that $\gamma^2=(g_{ij})$, then we get $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta-\gamma^{-1}\xi}_0^n},\quad \theta,\xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}. $$ we deduce from the change of variable $\hat{\xi}=\gamma^{-1}\xi$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}P(\kappa\theta,\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)&=&\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\gamma^{-1}\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)\cr &=&\frac{1}{\det\gamma}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\hat{\xi})(\det\gamma) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1 \end{eqnarray} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.18}). Let now $$ V_\theta=\set{\xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}_1,\,\,\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}\leq (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}}. $$ \begin{multline} \int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr \int_{V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1\backslash V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+4(1-\kappa)^{1/2}+(1-\kappa)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}, \end{multline} and then we get (\ref{4.19}).\\ By a simple computation, we have $$ \abs{\nabla_\xi^k P(\kappa\theta,\xi)}\leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^{n+k}},\quad k=1,2, $$ we deduce that \begin{equation} \norm{ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)}^2_{H^2(S_y\mathrm{M}_1)} \leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{(1-\kappa)^{n+4}}\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^n} d\omega_y(\xi)\leq \frac{C}{(1-\kappa)^{n+3}}. \end{equation} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.20}).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the Euclidean Poisson kernel via $\gamma=\sqrt{g}$; split the sphere near $\kappa\theta$ and differentiate the kernel.

nodes.name: Recall definitions
nodes.statement: We define the Poisson kernel of $B(0,1)\subset T_y \mathrm{M}_1$, i-e., $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\theta}^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\theta-\xi}^n},\quad \theta\in B(0,1);\,\, \xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}_1. $$ For $0<\kappa<1$, we define $\Psi_\kappa: S_y\mathrm{M}_1\times S_y\mathrm{M}_1\to \mathbb{R}$ as $$ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi)=P(\kappa\theta,\xi). $$

nodes.name: Euclidean Poisson kernel
nodes.statement: Let $P_0$ the Poisson kernel for the Euclidian unit ball $B_0(0,1)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ i.e., $$ P_0(\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi})=\frac{1-\abs{\hat{\theta}}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\hat{\theta}-\hat{\xi}}_0^n},\quad \hat{\theta}\in B_0(0,1);\,\, \hat{\xi}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$ where $\abs{\cdot}_0$ is the Euclidian norm of $\mathbb{R}^n$. From the well known properties of $P_0$, we have $$ \int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\hat{\theta},\hat{\xi}) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1, \quad\textrm{for all}\, \kappa\in (0,1),\,\, \hat{\theta}\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}. $$

nodes.name: Proof of (4.18)
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma=\sqrt{\mathrm{g}}:=(\gamma_{ij})$ be definite symetric positive matrix such that $\gamma^2=(g_{ij})$, then we get $$ P(\theta,\xi)=\frac{1-\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta}_0^2}{\alpha_n\abs{\gamma^{-1}\theta-\gamma^{-1}\xi}_0^n},\quad \theta,\xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}. $$ we deduce from the change of variable $\hat{\xi}=\gamma^{-1}\xi$ \begin{eqnarray} \int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}P(\kappa\theta,\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)&=&\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\gamma^{-1}\xi)d\omega_y(\xi)\cr &=&\frac{1}{\det\gamma}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}P_0(\kappa\gamma^{-1}\theta,\hat{\xi})(\det\gamma) d\omega_0(\hat{\xi})=1 \end{eqnarray} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.18}).

nodes.name: Proof of (4.19)
nodes.statement: Let now $$ V_\theta=\set{\xi\in S_y\mathrm{M}_1,\,\,\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}\leq (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}}. $$ \begin{multline} \int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr \int_{V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1\backslash V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+4(1-\kappa)^{1/2}+(1-\kappa)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n}, \end{multline} and then we get (\ref{4.19}).

nodes.statement: \int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)\leq\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr \int_{V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1\backslash V_\theta}\Psi_\kappa(\theta,\xi) \abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}d\omega_y(\xi)+(1-\kappa)\cr (1-\kappa)^{1/2n}+4(1-\kappa)^{1/2}+(1-\kappa)\leq C(1-\kappa)^{1/2n},
nodes.label: A.2

nodes.name: Proof of (4.20)
nodes.statement: By a simple computation, we have $$ \abs{\nabla_\xi^k P(\kappa\theta,\xi)}\leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^{n+k}},\quad k=1,2, $$ we deduce that \begin{equation} \norm{ \Psi_\kappa(\theta,\cdot)}^2_{H^2(S_y\mathrm{M}_1)} \leq C\frac{1-\kappa^2}{(1-\kappa)^{n+4}}\int_{S_y\mathrm{M}_1}\frac{1-\kappa^2}{\abs{\kappa\theta-\xi}^n} d\omega_y(\xi)\leq \frac{C}{(1-\kappa)^{n+3}}. \end{equation} This complete the proof of (\ref{4.20}).
